title: Poor Alignment and Steerability of Large Language Models: Evidence from College Admission Essays

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the pairwise cosine similarity of sentence embeddings and lexical features between LLM-generated essays (with and without identity prompting) and actual college admission essays authored by male and female applicants.

Measuring semantic alignment and pairwise cosine similarity between LLM-generated text and human-authored essays across different racial and ethnic groups (Asian, Black, White, Latino, American Indian/Pacific Islander).

Evaluating text similarity and lexical alignment of LLM-generated essays against human essays based on first-generation versus continuing-generation college student status, which serves as a proxy for socioeconomic background.

Prompting LLMs with the applicant's geographic location (e.g., U.S. state or international country) and analyzing whether the generated essays align with the linguistic patterns of human applicants from those specific regions.
